title: On tree-decompositions for infinite chordal graphs
summary: A graph is chordal if it contains no induced cycle of length four or more. While finite chordal graphs are precisely those admitting tree-decompositions into cliques, this fails for infinite graphs. We establish two results extending the known theory to the infinite setting. Our first result strengthens sufficient conditions of Halin, Kříž-Thomas, and Chudnovsky-Nguyen-Scott-Seymour: We show that every chordal graph without a strict comb of cliques admits a tree-decomposition into maximal cliques.
